_why: Every way into this repository is declared here once: what it is, who owns it, whether it is the authoritative surface, and where its code lives. scripts/entry_point_ratchet.py fails when a repository-root Python file, a services/ project, a SmsWorkbench project or a packaged artifact appears without a row, and when a row names something that no longer exists. That is the gate that stops entry points from accumulating at the root one convenience script at a time.
_rules: kind is one of kinds; status is one of statuses.
Every root-level *.py file is claimed by exactly one entry via roots.
Every services/<dir>/ and every SmsWorkbench* project directory is claimed.
Every declared root must exist (a row for deleted code fails).
Packaged artifacts (*.exe/*.msi/*.zip/*.7z) may not sit at the repository root; releases are built into dist/.
A new entry needs a row here AND a heading in docs/current/entry-points.md before it can land.

entries.purpose: The only supported command surface: argparse entry, lazy command dispatch and the early exits (--doctor, --desktop-serve, --pack-*).
The WPF shell. It plans commands and starts the Python backend; it owns no provider or protocol behaviour.
Historical entry name kept so old shortcuts and documentation keep working. Delegates to sms_tool.cli; add nothing here.
Standalone SOCKS5 listener that rotates over SOCKS5/HTTP-CONNECT upstreams, for local proxy-pool experiments.
Read-only proxy reachability check, optionally against the ChatGPT login edge (clean/blocked/degraded/dead).
Optional local mailbox/OTP helper service. Exposes an HTTP boundary and must not write the account store.
The protocol-payment extractors, one directory per payment method. A separate process on purpose: Boundary Rule 10 forbids importing sms_tool from here.
Gates, ratchets, scaffolds and one-off operator helpers, invoked by filename from CI, the git hooks and tests. New tooling goes here, never at the repository root.
The only supported build path for the desktop artifact and the installer (dist/ and dist/release/ outputs).

gate.purpose: Read-only gates, ratchets and guards. CI, the git hooks or a pytest wrapper invoke them by filename; a non-zero exit is a red build. None of them may write to the tree.

report.purpose: Generate a committed artefact (a doc, a graph, a reference table). They write, so they are run deliberately and their output is reviewed as a diff.

operator.purpose: Operational helpers that touch credentials, accounts, mailboxes or the network. Read the script before running it; several need an explicit flag to do anything destructive.

build.purpose: Build, packaging, runtime staging and environment setup.

refactor.purpose: Rewrite source. Each takes paths and rewrites them, so it is a reviewed act with the diff read afterwards, never a CI step.

scaffold.purpose: Generate a new unit of the platform.

package.purpose: Package marker, not a tool. It exists so the gates can be imported as ``scripts.x`` by their pytest wrappers.
